newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz says peso slide no cause for alarm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz says peso slide no cause for alarm.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said the peso's recent slide "is no cause for alarm", La Jornada newspaper reported Saturday.

The currency's 48-hour rate closed Friday at between 7.94 and 7.946 to the dollar, partially recouping from a dizzying 17.6 centavo slide Thursday. Its current level is well down from the 7.80 mark where it had traded most of the year.

In an interview with La Jornada on Saturday, Ortiz attributed the peso's sudden drop to normal, healthy fluctuations as well as nervousness over the U.S. certification of Mexico's drug-fighting efforts.
"The markets looked for a pretext to make an adjustment, but there is no cause for alarm or concern," he was quoted as saying.
Ortiz said the peso's depreciation will raise Mexico's interest payments on dollar-denominated debt, but will also increase the nation's income from crude oil exports.
"The petroleum income exceeds the interest payments and public sector imports. It may be small, but there is a surplus," he added.
He said capital is not fleeing the country, as was the case when the peso was devalued in December 1994.
"If at a given moment the peso lags expectations ... then the peso adjusts itself in steps, and this is normal and part of the banking system," Ortiz said.
